reviewPolicy.sourcePolicy: Use cited Element 189/190 definitions for required presence, the 3-digit representation, the value domain, and the relation to the following data field.
reviewPolicy.dataPolicy: The mismatch vectors are field-level designs reusing an existing reviewed-only Test data value by reference; they are not full converter-ready EMV requests.
reviewPolicy.baselinePolicy: References BR-RULE-SEG130-R-007 and existing authored EMV Test records; no rule or record is added to the official baseline.
reviewPolicy.promotionGate: Authorized Test review must confirm byte/count semantics, TLV validity, transaction applicability, fixture identity, expected validation, and readiness.

requirementReferences.title: EMV Chip Data Length (Element 189) is required and identifies the length of the following EMV Chip Data field; valid values 000-999
EMV Chip Data shall begin with a valid three-digit length consistent with the following encoded chip data.
EMV Chip Data shall preserve valid BCD-packed/hex TLV tag, length, and value structure.

sourceEvidence.quote: Number: 189 Name: EMV Chip Data Length Character Type: N Maximum Length: 3 bytes Representation: Fixed length of three digits Purpose: Identifies the length of the following field, EMV Chip Data, in an EMV transaction request and response. Processing Rules: Required in all EMV transactions. Valid Codes/Values: 000—999
sourceEvidence.interpretation: Element 189 is a required three-digit field in EMV transactions; its value identifies the following Element 190 field length and must lie in the stated range.

sourceEvidence.quote: Number: 190 Name: EMV Chip Data Character Type: ANSB Maximum Length: 999 bytes Representation: Variable length of 999 characters, preceded by three digit length indicator
sourceEvidence.interpretation: Element 190 is required and follows the three-digit length indicator; a non-empty Element 190 value cannot be described by a zero length.
The example presents a three-digit length and BCD-packed/hex data; exact encoding/count semantics for the draft vectors still require Test-owner confirmation.

aiReviewReferences.aiStatement: EMV Chip Data Length valid values are 000-999.
aiReviewReferences.interpretation: The value 000 is within Element 189's documented domain, but these payload observations do not demonstrate the length relationship because both pair it with non-empty Element 190 data. Neither case is a confirmed positive chain for the full Test rule.
aiReviewReferences.responseOracle: No host response outcome is inferred from these fields.

testScenarios.intent: Check that the required three-digit Element 189 identifies the following Element 190 length in a valid Segment 130 EMV request. Reuse the existing authored positive vector by reference and add reviewed mismatch mutations.

testCases.assertion: Element 189 is 000 while the referenced Element 190 contains the non-empty 10-byte value; the length indicator does not identify the following data length.
Element 189 is 011 while the referenced Element 190 contains the 10-byte value; the length indicator exceeds the following data length by one.

openQuestions: Confirm whether the Element 189 indicator counts encoded bytes, characters, or another wire-level unit for the supplied EMV Chip Data representation.
Confirm that the referenced 10-byte vector is valid for the applicable EMV request context and that the tested data remains unchanged in the mutations.
Define the independent source-conformance oracle for mismatched length indicators; no host response code is specified by the cited source.
